title: WHO IRIS — Institutional Repository for Information Sharing
sizeBasis: TWO SOURCES, both read 2026-09-20 off captures the owner supplied. (1) iris.who.int/statistics storage report, By Location, Entire Site: 'Nb of files: 1,057,223', 'Storage used: 361.55 GB', 'Nb of top-level communities: 8'. (2) iris.who.int/home, the search placeholder: “Search through the repository’s 273559 items”. ITEMS AND FILES ARE NOW SEPARATE FIELDS. `totalItemsUpstream` used to hold the FILE count, labelled as such, because the statistics page publishes files and not items and a guessed item count would have been worse than a labelled wrong one. The home page publishes the item count, so each has its own field: 273,559 items across 1,057,223 files is 3.86 files per item, which lands inside the 3-4x range the bundle structure predicted before either number was known. `totalBytesUpstream` IS DERIVED, NOT TRANSCRIBED: the report prints a 2-decimal figure and no byte count, so this is round(361.55 * 1024^3) and is therefore precise to about ±5 MiB. GiB rather than GB because that is the reading that round-trips every per-community figure the same report prints -- Headquarters' 238.58, AFRO's 19.72, EURO's 34.84, EMRO's 26.14 and WPRO's 25.71 all reproduce exactly at 2^30 and none of them does at 10^9. THE VALUE THIS REPLACES: 388,225,126,400, which claimed in this very field to be 361.55 * 1024^3 and was not -- it renders as 361.56 GiB, so every page built from it disagreed with the source note beside it by 0.01. The community figures were right all along; only the site total failed to round-trip its own stated basis. THE FIGURE ALL OF THIS REPLACES: every earlier note in this branch said '0.7 TB', which came from a chat message and was never measured.

sourceLoss.container: LOST WITH THE SOURCE. A container node holds a title, a child count and an upstream URL; none of what it lists is held here. If IRIS goes away the node survives only as a record that the collection existed. No Handle is recorded for any container yet (DSpace mints them upstream; none has been read), so it resolves only through the host.
sourceLoss.referencedItem: METADATA SURVIVES, BYTES DO NOT. A referenced item keeps its node and, where one is held, its folio-dublin-core/v1 record; its files were never copied and are lost with the source unless a web-archive snapshot exists. A snapshot is recorded only once verified (bun run check:source-liveness asks the Wayback Machine); an unverified pointer is not recorded.
sourceLoss.materializedItem: THE ARCHIVAL COPY SURVIVES. A materialized item's bytes are held with a recorded sha256 (its sourceLoss gate); fixity, not re-fetch, is how the copy is kept honest (refresh-materialized.bpmn, archival branch). Its Handle, where recorded, resolves the citation even after the host is gone.
